paper_metadata.title: Phase stability and microstructure evolution in a ductile refractory high entropy alloy Al10Nb15Ta5Ti30Zr40

evidence.quote: This paper reports the microstructural evolution and phase stability in a newly developed low -density Al 10Nb15Ta5Ti30Zr40 refractory high entropy alloy (RHEA) at different temperatures.
A novel low-density RHEA has been developed with the composition Al 10Nb15Ta5Ti30Zr40, exhibiting a unique nano-scale two-phase mixture of ordered B2 and disordered BCC.

The alloy was prepared by vacuum induction melting of high purity elements followed by suction casting in rods of ~13 mm in diameter and 55 mm in length.

To produce A+WQ condition, a cast rod was plac ed in a quartz tube, which was vacuumed, filled with high purity argon and fire-sealed. The tube with the sample was then placed in a furnace preheated to 1100°C, held at the temperature for 24 h and then water quenched.

other.cooling_rate: 20°C/min or furnace cooling, whichever is slower

evidence.quote: To produce A+ SC condition, cast samples were wrapped in a Ta foil and placed in a vacuum furnace. After the vacuum of 2x10 -3 Pa was reached, the samples were heated to a temperature of 1100°C at the heating rate of 50°C/min, held at the temperature for 24 hou rs and cooled at the cooling rate of 20°C/min or furnace cooling, whichever is slower.
